Time2Route: Build the Route Worth Taking

Alexander Semenov June 2026 6 min read
Open full screen
Not just A to B. Build the route worth taking.

Time2Route combines route planning, interesting places, stops, elevation profiles, and shareable links — all built around your route.

Your route, planned your way

Every route is a sequence of decisions. Here is how Time2Route turns a direction into a journey.

Walk or bike — different route, different feel

Time2Route supports two travel modes. Switching the mode rebuilds the route with different constraints and gives you a more realistic plan for the way you'll actually move.

Walking vs cycling — same start/end, different route.

Interesting places near the route line

Time2Route finds places in relation to the route you just built — not as scattered city-wide pins. Coffee shops just off the path, a viewpoint 200 metres from your cycling route, a park that splits your walk into two comfortable halves. The route is the filter.

Click a place on the map or in the list, inspect it, then add it as a stop.

Stops on the route

A stop transforms a direction into a plan. Add a coffee break, a viewpoint, a park bench — the route recalculates around each stop, and the timeline shifts from A→B to a small itinerary.

Start → Destination
→
Start → coffee → park → viewpoint → Destination

Elevation that is easy to read

Distance and duration tell you how long. Elevation tells you how it will feel. One glance at the profile and you know where the effort is.

Avoid surprise climbs.
See steep sections before you start — no hidden hills mid-route.
Choose scenic effort.
A climb to a viewpoint looks different from a climb through a tunnel. Pick the one worth it.
Understand the route before you go.
Total ascent, max grade, rolling vs punchy — the profile tells the story in one glance.

Route parameters in the URL

Every route in Time2Route is encoded directly in the URL. A prepared route link embeds the start, destination, stops, mode, and options — no server-side storage, no sign-up required. Open the link, and the route is already there.

Why URL parameters?

Route URL routes work everywhere a link works:

  • Shared in newsletters, route collections, and travel guides
  • Embedded in social media posts and blog articles
  • Sent as a personal recommendation — "here's the route I took"
  • Opened on any device, no login required

Build a route worth taking

Start anywhere. Add a stop. Check the elevation. Share the link. Your first route is waiting.
